97056806.b:
In the heart of Baljurashi governorate stands the historic Saturday Market, one of the oldest and largest traditional markets in the Al Baha region, preserving its authentic spirit and details for centuries. It is not just a place to shop but a living cultural landmark that documents the features of daily life and the traditions passed down by local people through generations.

The scent of aromatic herbs and the voices of vendors drift toward you as you wander the market's narrow aisles, where handicrafts, traditional fabrics, local products and heritage tools are displayed. Every corner here tells a story from the good old days.

With its vernacular architecture, warm atmosphere and honest identity, the market invites you on a complete sensory journey that expresses the depth of heritage and the spirit of the south.

The market has been held in the same place for about four centuries, and has a small museum and shops selling handicrafts and the local honey for which the Al Baha region is famous.

97042223.s: Historical Quba Castle sits on a small hill in the Al Duwaimah district of Madinah, near Quba Mosque. It dates back more than 100 years, and was built as a guard post overlooking the route of pilgrims coming to Madinah and protecting the area from attacks by tribes and bandits. The castle reflects the journey of transformation from defense to peace through the history of Madinah, and is today one of the most prominent heritage landmarks that the Tourism and National Heritage Authority is keen to restore and preserve within Madinah's historic routes, visited by those interested in antiquities and the history of Madinah.
97042223.b:
Historical Quba Castle sits on a small hill in the Al Duwaimah district of Madinah, near Quba Mosque. It dates back more than 100 years, and was built as a guard post overlooking the route of pilgrims coming to Madinah and protecting the area from attacks by tribes and bandits.

The castle reflects the journey of transformation from defense to peace through the history of Madinah, and is today one of the most prominent heritage landmarks that the Tourism and National Heritage Authority is keen to restore and preserve within Madinah's historic routes, visited by those interested in antiquities and the history of Madinah.

The Quba area in general is one of the most prominent historic sites in Madinah, and is linked to many important Islamic events since the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him), forming an important part of the city's historical and cultural identity. The area is also close to a number of well-known Islamic sites, making it an important stop on visiting routes and cultural tourism.

The village's history goes back several centuries, and it has witnessed many important events that helped shape its cultural identity. Zabna is known for its traditional architectural houses and narrow alleys that reflect the old way of life.

94902797.t: The Kiswa Factory of the Holy Ka'aba
94902797.s: Saudi Arabia began its journey of caring for the weaving of the Kiswa of the Holy Kaaba in the era of the founding King Abdulaziz bin Abdulrahman Al Saud in 1927, when he opened a house specialized in making the Kiswa in Makkah, which produced the first Saudi Kiswa for the Kaaba.
94902797.b:
The story of the Kiswa factory

Saudi Arabia began its journey of caring for the weaving of the Kiswa of the Holy Kaaba in the era of the founding King Abdulaziz bin Abdulrahman Al Saud in 1927, when he opened in his reign a house specialized in making the Kiswa in Makkah, which produced the first Saudi Kiswa for the Kaaba. It then moved to the "Kaaba Kiswa Factory" in 1977 in Umm Al Joud, one of the districts of Makkah.

The sons of King Abdulaziz followed the making and development of the Kiswa with great attention and care to this day. In the reign of King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, the doors of modernization and renewal were opened to the electronic systems, mechanical equipment and electrical devices at the Kaaba Kiswa Factory. In the reign of King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, the name changed to become "King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswa of the Holy Kaaba", and the complex is supervised by the General Presidency for the Affairs of the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque.

A tour of the complex

Visiting the complex is a rich opportunity to see one of the largest facilities specialized in silk weaving and embroidery, and to see the work steps of about 200 specialist technicians and administrators completing this magnificent garment.

You will learn about the history of the complex, the stages of making the Kiswa of the Kaaba, and how it is replaced. The complex includes several departments, including: the dye house, mechanical weaving, hand weaving, printing, the belt, gilding, sewing, and Kiswa assembly.

Replacing the Kiswa of the Kaaba

Eyes used to eagerly await the ceremony of the Kaaba being clothed in its new garment each year, after the dawn prayer on the ninth day of Dhul Hijjah. However, in 1444 AH / 2022 CE, the date of replacing the Kiswa of the Kaaba changed, and it became the first of the month of Muharram.

Visiting times

The complex welcomes its Muslim visitors to a unique educational experience between the weaving and embroidery of the Kiswa of the Kaaba. Individuals can go to the site and book, while companies and groups belonging to a pilgrim group must book through the website of the General Authority for the Care of the Affairs of the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque.
